subject: Regional surcharge allocation & tax handling question for EU residency adders
messages:
From: Alex Martin <cloudworks-sales@cloudworks.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marie Dubois <marie.dubois@floomedia.eu>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 16:14:00 +00:00
Subject: Question on how EU residency adders will appear on invoices and VAT treatment

Hi Jonas,

We are preparing an internal cost model for FlooMedia and want to understand how Redwood will present multi-region pricing on the invoice. Two quick clarifications:

1) If we choose EU data residency for some flows, will the residency adder be shown as a separate line item per usage record (per API call / token) or as a monthly allocation line on the invoice?

2) Does Redwood net or gross the EU surcharge with respect to VAT? For our finance team we need to know whether the adder will be subject to VAT or treated as a pass-through.

I attached the ratecard you sent last month — we have highlighted the residency rows that concern us.

Can you confirm the presentation and whether we should expect any local tax implications to be surfaced on the invoice?

Thanks,
Alex
CloudWorks (partner for FlooMedia)
Attachment: Redwood-Ratecard-2027-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet, 84KB)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martin <cloudworks-sales@cloudworks.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on how EU residency adders will appear on invoices and VAT treatment

Alex — thanks for the clear questions, and for sending the highlighted ratecard. Looping in Laura and Sergio to confirm operational and billing behavior.

Short answers up front:
- Residency adders can be shown either as a per-usage line (token-level) or consolidated monthly as an "EU Residency Top-up" allocation — we support both depending on the account's billing granularity.
- VAT handling depends on the customer entity and whether we have a valid VAT ID on file. For EU-registered business customers with a valid VAT number, we generally inverse-charge the VAT (net). For B2C or customers without VAT registration, VAT is applied gross.

Details / ask for internal confirmation: is the account opting for token-level billing in HubSpot (they indicated yes in the deal) or monthly consolidation? If consolidated, we need to ensure the billing exports tag the EU top-up to the correct tax code so finance can apply VAT correctly.

I'll draft a short note back to Alex with both presentation options and recommended language for their finance team. Laura / Sergio — any constraints from billing ops or legal on line-item wording and tax code mapping?

—Jonas
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on how EU residency adders will appear on invoices and VAT treatment

Jonas / Sergio — quick ops note:

1) Billing presentation options:
   - Token-level: line per invoice detail with code RES-EU, show usage units and per-token adder.
   - Consolidated: single monthly line "EU Residency Top-up (RES-EU)" with total amount.

2) Tax mapping:
   - If customer provides valid EU VAT ID in billing profile -> reverse charge, we flag tax_exempt = true and invoice shows net amounts with a reference note "VAT reverse-charged per EU VAT rules".
   - If no VAT ID or consumer entity -> VAT applied per billing country (we use customer billing address to determine EU VAT rate).

3) Suggested invoice language for consolidated line (clean for finance):
   "EU Residency Top-up (RES-EU) — Additional charge for data residency and processing in EU regions; taxed per customer billing profile."

4) Implementation notes: our invoicing export (CSV) uses tax_code, tax_rate, and allocation_tag columns. For FlooMedia/CloudWorks deal please ensure HubSpot has the billing VAT and billing country fields populated; otherwise tax will auto-apply as gross.

I also recommend we include an SOW line that clarifies residency selection and billing method to avoid surprises during renewal. Draft attached for review.

Attachments: SOW-draft-FlooMedia-20270413.pdf

—Laura
Sr. Billing Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martin <cloudworks-sales@cloudworks.com>, Marie Dubois <marie.dubois@floomedia.eu>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on how EU residency adders will appear on invoices and VAT treatment

Alex / Marie — thanks for the patience. Quick consolidated response and recommended next steps for FlooMedia's procurement team: 

1) Presentation option (select one):
   a) Token-level detail — each usage row will include a RES-EU adder line item. Recommended if you want granular usage reconciliation.
   b) Monthly consolidated — a single line "EU Residency Top-up (RES-EU)" that aggregates the month. This reduces volume on your AP system.

2) VAT / tax handling:
   - If FlooMedia provides a valid EU VAT ID we will apply reverse-charge (net). Please upload the VAT ID to your billing profile in our portal or provide it to your procurement contact and we will validate.
   - If no VAT ID, VAT will be charged based on billing country. We'll show tax lines on the invoice so your finance team can reconcile.

3) Attachment and SOW: Attached is the highlighted ratecard you sent plus a short SOW paragraph we propose to add to the contract that calls out the selected presentation option. If you prefer the consolidated monthly top-up, we will tag invoices with tax_code = RES-EU and send a monthly CSV export to your accounting system.

Next steps: please confirm (i) which presentation you prefer and (ii) whether FlooMedia will provide a VAT ID. Once confirmed we'll update HubSpot and send a final SOW paragraph for signature.

Best,
Jonas
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
